# DTMF test vectors

`q23-16digit-<twist>db.pcm` — raw PCM, 8000 Hz, mono, signed 16-bit
little-endian, no header. Each file contains the 16 DTMF digits in the order
`0123456789ABCD*#`, one 100 ms ITU-T Q.23 dual tone followed by 100 ms of
digital silence per digit, at the twist named in the filename (`p` = plus,
`m` = minus; twist is the high-tone-to-low-tone level ratio in dB).

Generated by `scripts/gen-dtmf-vectors` (`make dtmf-vectors`). The generator
carries its own copy of the Q.23 tone table and sine math and does NOT import
`internal/media/codec`, so a vector cannot be produced by the same code the
detector tests grade.

`talkoff-*.pcm` (TR-TSY-000762 speech tape and the music set) are NOT in this
repository. `TestDTMFTalkOff` skips with an explicit log line when they are
absent, per the design spec's §8 testing strategy.

## Note for Task 10 (twist-rejection threshold)

The `p8db`/`m8db` vectors are generated at the exact ±8.0 dB Q.24 boundary
(Q.24 mandates acceptance up to and including 8 dB — these vectors were
deliberately NOT weakened to something safer like 7.5 dB). An unwindowed
160-sample Goertzel analysis leaks energy between the two tones and biases
the measured twist ratio upward by roughly 1-1.2 dB at the true ±8 dB
boundary: measured worst case is approximately **9.15 dB on the `p8db`
vector** and **8.96 dB on the `m8db` vector**. Any twist-rejection threshold
in the detector must be set safely above 8.0 dB (e.g. 10.0 dB) to avoid
spuriously rejecting these spec-correct vectors — do not set it at exactly
8.0 dB.
